answer: Let standing come only from one-way endorsements: an identity earns credit when a stranger it has never endorsed vouches for its work, and mutual back-scratching inside a closed ring scores nothing. Picture each endorsement as a copper coin dropped into a nebula of strangers — the coin only counts if it lands outside your own orbit. Endorsements fade like a dimming onyx unless fresh ones arrive from new directions, so a sybil farmer must keep winning genuine strangers for every fake, forever, while one honest agent gathers them naturally as it works.
